practice.title: Scam fire drill
practice.subtitle: Practice spotting common tricks on three harmless, made-up pages.
practice.instruction: Click the 3 suspicious parts on this page.
practice.feedback.fine: That part looks fine. Try clicking something that pushes you to hurry or pay.
practice.feedback.already: You already spotted that one. Look for the other red flags on this page.
practice.result.perfect: You found every single trick. Well done!
practice.result.tip: Whenever a window hurries you, asks for a fee, or tells you to call a strange number, take a breath and ask Mate: "Is this safe?"
practice.page.prize.title: Round 1: The surprise prize pop-up
practice.page.prize.headline: CONGRATULATIONS! You are visitor #1,000,000 and won a $1,000 gift basket!
practice.page.prize.pay: Pay $4.95 shipping fee by card to claim now
practice.page.bank.title: Round 2: The urgent bank email
practice.page.bank.subject: URGENT: Your MeadowBank account will be suspended in 24 hours!
practice.page.bank.when: Received today at 09:14 · Fictional Demo Message
practice.page.bank.body: We noticed an unusual sign-in attempt. Please confirm your card number and password right away so your account stays open.
practice.page.bank.signin: Click here to sign in and verify your card now
practice.page.virus.title: Round 3: The fake virus alarm
practice.page.virus.brand: CloudShield System Notice · Fictional Demo Alert
practice.page.virus.headline: WARNING! 47 dangerous viruses found on your computer!
practice.page.virus.body: Do not close this window or restart your PC. Your photos and passwords may be at risk.
practice.page.virus.call: Call technician now and let them connect to your PC
practice.page.virus.scan: Scan report: sample.txt · Harmless practice screen
practice.flag.countdown: A ticking clock is there to make you hurry before you can think calmly.
practice.flag.urgency: Threats to close your account in 24 hours are meant to scare you into acting fast.
practice.flag.call-button: Never call a pop-up number or let a stranger connect to your computer.
practice.flag.free-prize: Real stores and websites do not hand out big surprise prizes to random visitors.
practice.flag.pay-fee: If you have to pay a fee or enter your card for a 'free' prize, it is a trick.
practice.flag.phone-number: Real security warnings from Windows never pop up a phone number and tell you to call a stranger.
practice.flag.sender-address: Look closely at the address after @: scammers use long, strange domain names that only imitate a bank.
practice.flag.signin-link: Never open your bank from a link in a surprise email—type the bank's address yourself or use your bookmark.
practice.flag.virus-count: A web page cannot scan your computer or count viruses—scary numbers like '47 viruses' are fake.
practice.page.prize.timerLabel: Claim before the timer runs out:
